title: Optimize - Smart Routing (beta) launch messaging & competitive notes
content:
Overview:

A short, practical launch pack for Redwood Optimize: Smart Routing (beta). Smart Routing is a policy-driven request router that automatically balances latency, cost, and quality by sending inference requests to the best-available model variant, region, or capacity tier. This doc contains positioning, core messages, target segments, competitive notes, an announcement draft, internal talk tracks, and a short demo script for sales/solutions enablement.

Why we built it (one-liner):
Make production inference resilient and cost-predictable by routing requests to the optimal compute and model variant without engineering work.

Topline customer benefit (headline):
Cut per-request cost up to 35% and reduce outage impact with automated, policy-driven routing — all while preserving SLA-level quality.

Key value props (3 bullets):
- Cost-aware routing: Automatically prefer cheaper model variants and lower-cost regions when quality delta is within a customer-defined tolerance.
- SLA-first fallbacks: Route around capacity or region failures to maintain latency/availability targets with automatic graceful degradation.
- Zero-instrumentation policy controls: Teams set simple policies (latency SLO, quality deviation tolerance, cost cap) — Redwood Optimize enforces and reports on them.

Primary target personas (who to sell to):
- Platform/Infra teams (SRE, platform engineers): care about reliability, predictable cost, and operational simplicity.
- ML/Model Ops: care about quality control, evaluation and can set model quality thresholds.
- Product engineering (high-volume customers): need predictable latency at scale and want to reduce inference spend.

Key use cases to call out:
- Multi-region customer with strict latency SLAs that wants to degrade to secondary region while maintaining acceptable output quality.
- Companies using expensive high-accuracy models for a subset of traffic and cheaper variants for bulk predictions.
- Teams running mixed private/dedicated/hosted deployments who want unified routing across environments.

Core messages and proof points (for landing pages, sales decks):
- Message: "Smarter requests, lower bill, fewer incidents."
  - Proof point: Internal pilot with three customers showed 18–35% cost savings (Q1 pilot average 24%) with no measurable drop in NLU task F1 when tolerance set to 1–2%.
- Message: "Policy-first routing for production-grade inference."
  - Proof point: Policy engine is integrated into rollout plane; customers can canary routing rules and rollback automatically; RBAC on policies.
- Message: "Unified across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
  - Proof point: Same API controls and telemetry across regions and capacity tiers; customers can pin certain tenants to private instances.

Competitive analysis (short notes):
- Major cloud vendors (A, B): Offer endpoint failover and region routing but lack model-quality-aware routing and per-request cost governance. Their failovers are infra-first, not model-quality-first.
- Inference infrastructure vendors (X, Y): Provide advanced routing/orchestration but require heavy operator code and customized agents. Our differentiator is a simple policy layer and out-of-the-box metrics tied to model evaluation sets.
- Niche startups (Z): Claim auto-tiering; usually focused on batching and cost only. They often require model conversion and don't support private deployments or precise quality thresholds.

Competitive positioning statement (single paragraph):
Redwood Optimize — Smart Routing sits between cloud infra failover and bespoke routing systems by offering a lightweight, policy-driven router that reasons about model quality, latency, and cost simultaneously. For engineering teams that must serve inference at scale, Smart Routing reduces spend and outage risk without additional operator overhead or vendor lock-in.

Launch plan & assets (timeline summary):
- Mar wk1: Finalize beta docs, sample policies, canary playbook (internal).
- Mar wk2: Invite 10 pilot customers (existing Dedicated/Private customers + high-volume hosted accounts).
- Mar wk3: Internal enablement: sales + SE training, playbooks, demo videos.
- Apr wk1: Public beta announcement (blog + product update), sample configs in SDK.
- Apr ongoing: Feedback loop, iterate on UI rule editor and analytics.

Assets to deliver:
- One-pager product brief (customer-facing)
- Sales playbook + objection handling doc
- Three short demo recordings (policy setup, failover simulation, cost savings dashboard)
- Post-pilot case study template
- Sample policy library (latency-first, cost-first, quality-first)

Internal enablement / sales talk tracks (short bullets):
- Opening: "Smart Routing lets you set SLOs — we do the rest. Want quality or cost? Pick tolerance and let Redwood route"
- Objection: "How do you measure quality?" -> "We tie routing decisions to an eval set and configurable delta thresholds; customers see per-policy quality telemetry and rollback capability."
- Objection: "What if routing introduces added latency?" -> "Routing decisions are made at the request gateway with cached routing tables; default routing adds sub-millisecond decision time. We also offer warm routing tables for cold-start-sensitive paths."

Demo script (3-min canary demo):
- Step 1: Show policy console — create policy: latency_SLO=50ms, quality_tolerance=2%, prefer_region=eu-west.
- Step 2: Start traffic: show baseline serving to eu-west high-accuracy model.
- Step 3: Simulate eu-west capacity drop: policy routes to eu-central cheaper model with 1.5% quality delta; latency remains within SLO.
- Step 4: Show cost dashboard: % of traffic routed to cheaper variant, estimated savings, and ability to revert policy.

Announcement draft (customer-facing email / blog bullets):
Subject: Try Smart Routing (beta) — lower inference cost and keep SLAs
Hi there,
We’re excited to invite you to the beta for Smart Routing, a new Redwood Optimize capability that automatically routes inference to the best combination of model, region, and capacity tier based on the policies you define. Early pilots cut inference spend by up to 35% while preserving model quality and availability.
What you can do today:
- Create policies that prioritize latency, cost, or quality
- Run canaries and automatic rollbacks
- Get per-policy telemetry and cost attribution
Sign up for the beta (link) — limited spots.

Internal quick FAQ (enablement):
Q: Who is eligible for the beta?
A: Customers on Dedicated or Private; selected Hosted customers with >$5k/mo inference spend.
Q: How is quality measured?
A: By applying a customer-provided or Redwood-provided eval set and calculating per-policy metric deltas (F1, accuracy, perplexity depending on task).
Q: What happens if a model’s output drifts after rollout?
A: We continuously compare outputs to the eval set and can auto-fallback to pinned model variants or pause routing rules.

Success metrics (pilot/KPI recommendations):
- Per-customer: % inference cost reduction (target 15–30% within 30 days)
- SLO compliance: % requests within latency SLO after routing (target 99.9% for latency-first policies)
- Quality delta: average metric delta vs baseline (target <2% for beta)
- Adoption: # customers enrolled in beta and # policies created per customer

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Surface-level quality metrics may not capture downstream task regressions.
  Mitigation: Emphasize per-customer eval sets and provide a "holdout production check" phase where we shadow route 5–10% and run end-to-end tests.
- Risk: Complexity of policy UI causes misconfigurations.
  Mitigation: Ship three opinionated templates and validation checks with recommended defaults.

Open questions / decisions needed (notes to PM):
- Beta eligibility thresholds and quota for hosted customers.
- Template policy gallery and naming conventions.
- Telemetry retention for per-policy analytics (30 days vs 90 days).

Next steps (first 10 days):
1) Ship beta docs + sample policies (owner: Product)
2) Align SE + Sales on canary playbook (owner: GTM)
3) Prepare SDK examples for Node/Python (owner: DevX)
4) Draft public blog + email copy for Apr 1 launch (owner: Marketing)

Notes to self: keep language simple for early customers; highlight low-risk ways to start (shadow mode, small traffic canaries). Link to internal pilot results and telemetry dashboards for talking points.
